--- title: 'OLS verification: R, statsmodels and PHP' jupyter: python3 --- This notebook fits exactly the same design matrices and outcomes with three implementations. This verification opts out of PHP intercept insertion (`intercept: false`), so PHP and statsmodels receive the same explicit design; R's formula below generates the same ones column. We use conventional covariance, Student t inference, 95% intervals, and Gaussian likelihood at the ML variance. See [setup](index.qmd), the [verification record](../verifications/ols.qmd), and the [math walkthrough](ols-math.qmd). ::: {#006eb774 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import sys import pandas as pd ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "Cargo.toml").exists()) sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "docs/verifications")) from compare_ols import cases, compare_case simple = next(case for case in cases() if case['name'] == 'simulated_housing') display(pd.DataFrame({'intercept': [row[0] for row in simple['x']], 'area_m2': [row[1] for row in simple['x']], 'monthly_rent': simple['y']})) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
intercept area_m2 monthly_rent
0 1 74.4 1879.25
1 1 57.4 1805.03
2 1 66.4 2022.29
3 1 49.1 1267.85
4 1 45.7 1509.24

6 1 37.0 959.51
7 1 93.9 2386.54
``` ::: ::: The displayed data are simulated apartments from the shared [housing CSV](../data/housing.csv). The math walkthrough explains the generating equation and sample correlations. The `simulated_housing_multiple` case also includes bedrooms: this predictor is strongly correlated with area, but the design remains full rank. Its generating coefficient is zero conditional on area; a sample estimate need not equal zero. ## Equivalent calls R, using the table above: ```r fit <- lm(monthly_rent ~ area_m2, data = observations, na.action = na.omit) summary(fit) confint(fit, level = 0.95) logLik(fit) ``` Python statsmodels: ```python fit = sm.OLS(y, X, missing='drop', hasconst=True).fit(use_t=True) fit.params, fit.bse, fit.tvalues, fit.pvalues, fit.conf_int(), fit.llf ``` PHP: ```php // missing defaults to 'drop' $result = Phit\fit_ols_matrix( x: $x, y: $y, intercept: false, ); ``` The executable harness uses `y ~ . - 1` in R with the explicit design columns to avoid inserting a second intercept. It calculates centered/uncentered R-squared explicitly because that formula is syntactically no-intercept even when the supplied matrix contains ones. All other quantities come from R's fitted model. This makes the same runner work for multiple and no-intercept designs. ::: {#41bcea91 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} simple_result = compare_case(simple) print(simple_result['versions']) rows = [] for name in ['R', 'statsmodels', 'phit']: result = simple_result[name] for i, label in enumerate(['intercept', 'area_m2']): rows.append({'implementation': name, 'term': label, 'coefficient': result['coefficients'][i], 'SE': result['std_errors'][i], 't': result['t_statistics'][i], 'p': result['p_values'][i], 'lower 95%': result['conf_int'][i][0], 'upper 95%': result['conf_int'][i][1]}) display(pd.DataFrame(rows)) display(pd.DataFrame([{ 'implementation': name, **{key: simple_result[name][key] for key in ['rss', 'sigma', 'df_residual', 'r_squared', 'adj_r_squared', 'log_likelihood']}} for name in ['R', 'statsmodels', 'phit']])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'R': 'R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24)', 'statsmodels': '0.15.0', 'numpy': '2.5.4', 'Python': '3.14.7', 'PHP': '8.5.10'} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Automated agreement, including row deletion The runner compares all statistical fields using `abs(actual-reference) <= 1e-9 + 1e-7*abs(reference)` and checks retained sample counts and row positions separately. It covers simple, multiple, correlated full-rank, and no-intercept cases. The missing-data case drops one predictor-missing row and one outcome-missing row: every implementation must use the same four observations. PHP's warning is captured and shown below. R's explicit `na.omit` and statsmodels' explicit `missing='drop'` select complete cases. They do not imply that all libraries warn on deletion by default. PHP deliberately emits a warning and returns metadata. ::: {#c6ef53c4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} results = [simple_result] + [compare_case(case) for case in cases() if case['name'] != 'simulated_housing'] summary = [] for result in results: largest_error = max(error for errors in result['max_absolute_errors_vs_R'].values() for error in errors.values()) summary.append({'case': result['name'], 'n input': result['phit']['n_input'], 'n retained': result['phit']['n_observations'], 'n dropped': result['phit']['n_dropped'], 'largest absolute difference vs R': largest_error}) display(pd.DataFrame(summary)) missing = next(result for result in results if result['name'] == 'listwise_missing') print('Dropped original positions:', missing['phit']['dropped_rows']) print('Retained original positions:', missing['phit']['retained_rows']) print('PHP warning:', missing['warnings'][0]['message']) print('All three implementations agree for every case and checked field.') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
case n input n retained n dropped largest absolute difference vs R
0 simulated_housing 8 8 0 8.731149e-11
1 simulated_housing_multiple 8 8 0 1.164153e-10
2 simple 5 5 0 1.065814e-13
3 multiple 10 10 0 3.552714e-14
4 no_intercept 10 10 0 4.263256e-14
5 correlated 10 10 0 2.870593e-12
6 listwise_missing 6 4 2 1.506351e-12
``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Dropped original positions: [1, 3] Retained original positions: [0, 2, 4, 5] PHP warning: Phit\fit_ols_matrix(): dropped 2 of 6 observations with missing values (listwise deletion) All three implementations agree for every case and checked field. ``` ::: ::: ## Limits The harness excludes perfect and zero fits from three-way finite comparisons: floating-point residuals can differ dramatically relative to their tiny magnitudes, and some inference is undefined. The Rust/PHP test suites cover those conventions separately. phit rejects singular designs, so they are not compared with references that alias coefficients. The tolerance includes an absolute floor; it does not promise relative accuracy for extremely small p-values. This notebook verifies these cases in the recorded environment, not every dataset or platform. See [Verification](../verification.qmd) for coverage and fixture maintenance. Sources: [R lm](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/lm.html), [statsmodels OLS](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.regression.linear_model.OLS.html), [statsmodels missing-data behavior](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/missing.html).
